art.subject: Long-billed Dowitcher (Limnodromus scolopaceus), adult in winter (non-breeding) plumage, as seen on Korean wetlands in late autumn: crown and upperparts plain dark grey with narrow paler feather edges; a clear whitish supercilium above a dark loral stripe; face, neck and breast fairly uniform pale grey-brown; breast sides and flanks with some dark bars; belly white; undertail coverts barred dark; bill blackish with a dull greenish-buff base; dark eye; legs yellowish-green.
art.pose: standing at the water's edge, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal mudflat at a river mouth with shallow pools in late autumn (October–November); no people, buildings or text
views: adult winter, side view standing in shallow water: very long straight bill with a pale base, plain dark grey upperparts with pale edges, whitish supercilium, pale grey-brown breast, dark bars on the breast sides and flanks, white belly, yellowish-green legs
adult, head detail in profile: long straight black bill with a dull greenish-buff base, whitish supercilium above a dark loral stripe, pale grey-brown face
adult, in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in line: dark grey wings with a narrow white trailing edge, white wedge from the rump up the back, finely barred tail
art.build: Medium-sized, stocky, snipe-like wader, 30cm, about Common Redshank size but heavier and shorter-necked, front-heavy with a hunched, horizontal stance. Bill very long and straight, about twice head length, with only a slight droop at the very tip. Legs medium length, yellowish-green. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a narrow white wedge runs from the rump up the lower back, the tail is finely barred blackish and white, and the secondaries have a narrow white trailing edge. Feeds by rapid vertical 'sewing-machine' probing.
avoid: Do not paint an upturned bill or long legs; that is a godwit.
Do not paint an all-black, blunt-tipped bill with long blackish legs; that is Asian Dowitcher (Limnodromus semipalmatus).
Do not show rufous underparts in the late-autumn scene; brick-red plumage is breeding plumage only.
Do not paint a snipe's striped crown and cryptic brown back; the winter upperparts are plain dark grey.
